use_when: To show how full something is against a known total, such as a property's occupancy for a night ("38 of 48 · 79%").
To compare parts of a whole side by side, such as revenue by booking channel, with each share as the Value.
To show a score out of a maximum, such as review scores by category; hide the label row when the layout already names it.
Use tone inverse on navy backgrounds, such as a sold-out night in the calendar.

dont_use_when.when: For steps in a flow, such as "1 of 3": use the Stepper component instead.
To compare exact figures across many rows: use the Table component instead.

a11y.fact: The component renders a native <progress> with max=100, so the progressbar role and value announcement are the browser's own.
The visible label is linked to the <progress> with aria-labelledby, using an id generated by React's useId.
When showLabel is false the label text is applied as aria-label so the progress bar keeps an accessible name.
The helper text is linked with aria-describedby when it is shown.
value is clamped to 0..100 (non-finite becomes 0) before it reaches the element and the value text.
